key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over minutes to hours. LOCATION: BILATERAL or unilateral. DURATION: Lasts minutes to hours. CHARACTER: DULL, ACHING, PRESSURE-like pain. AGGRAVATING: STRESS, tension, poor posture. RELIEVING: REST, relaxation, medications. TIMING: Gradual onset, lasts minutes to hours. SEVERITY: 3-6/10, mild to moderate. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: MILD nausea, may have neck tension, may have stress. KEY POSITIVES: Dull pain, bilateral distribution, stress triggers. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: Sudden severe headache - possible subarachnoid hemorrhage, call 911
Headache with neck stiffness and fever - possible meningitis, call 911
Headache with focal neurological deficits - possible stroke, call 911
Headache with signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Headache with severe hypertension - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
